events.title: C# 7 released with Visual Studio 2017
events.summary: Microsoft shipped Visual Studio 2017 on March 7, 2017 with C# 7 — adding pattern matching, tuples, and local functions.
events.about: C# 7's `is` patterns, `switch` expressions, and value tuples made data-oriented code concise. Out variables and ref returns closed gaps with modern languages — part of C#'s rapid evolution on Roslyn.

narrative.whyChosen: C# 7 brought algebraic-style patterns to millions of .NET developers.
narrative.whyImportant: Pattern matching influenced later C# versions and F# interoperability.
narrative.problemSolved: C# lacked concise destructuring and type tests for complex data shapes.

events.title: Lisa Su launches AMD Ryzen on Zen architecture
events.summary: AMD launched Ryzen processors on the Zen architecture on March 2, 2017 — ending years of Intel [CPU] dominance in desktop performance.
events.about: Under Lisa Su's leadership, Zen delivered competitive IPC and core counts at aggressive prices — reviving AMD in servers with EPYC and in gaming with Ryzen. It reshaped the x86 duopoly.

narrative.whyChosen: Zen was AMD's comeback architecture after the Bulldozer era.
narrative.whyImportant: Competitive CPUs lowered cloud and [PC] costs and accelerated innovation.
narrative.problemSolved: AMD had fallen behind Intel on performance per watt and market share.

events.title: CSS Grid Layout ships in Firefox 52
events.summary: Mozilla enabled unprefixed CSS Grid Layout in Firefox 52 on March 7, 2017 — the first major browser to ship the two-dimensional layout module.
events.about: CSS Grid lets authors define rows, columns, and named areas with `display: grid` and `grid-template-areas` — replacing float hacks and framework grid systems for page-level layout. Chrome 57 followed a week later; by late 2017 every major browser supported Grid, ending a decade of table and flexbox workarounds for two-dimensional designs.

narrative.whyChosen: CSS Grid was the biggest layout advance since flexbox — and Firefox shipped it first.
narrative.whyImportant: It gave the web a native two-dimensional layout system designed for [UI] and page design.
narrative.problemSolved: Complex page layouts required nested flexbox containers, floats, or JavaScript grid libraries.

events.title: Microsoft Teams launches worldwide
events.summary: Microsoft made Teams generally available worldwide on March 14, 2017 — chat, meetings, and Office 365 integrations positioned as Slack's enterprise rival.
events.about: Teams bundled video, channels, and SharePoint tabs into every Office 365 license — winning enterprises already standardized on Microsoft. GitHub, Azure [DevOps], and Planner integrations targeted engineering orgs; COVID remote work cemented Teams alongside Zoom as the default corporate communication stack.

narrative.whyChosen: Teams bundled chat into Office 365 and challenged Slack in the enterprise.
narrative.whyImportant: Tight Microsoft integration made it the default for Fortune 500 engineering departments.
narrative.problemSolved: Enterprises paying for Office wanted chat without buying a separate Slack contract.
